personas.description: You build OmniScripts, FlexCards and Integration Procedures on industry cloud projects.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the OmniStudio Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: It is a moderate exam, but OmniStudio works unlike the rest of Salesforce. The tools are configured rather than coded, and the questions test whether you know which tool does which job and how data moves between them.
bullets: About 72% to pass, roughly 39 correct answers out of 60. Confirm it in the official exam guide before you book.
Tool choice. Most questions come down to picking the right one of four tools for a job.
Hands-on helps. If you have built and debugged an OmniScript that calls an Integration Procedure, much of this is familiar.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build one OmniScript that reads data with a Data Mapper, calls an Integration Procedure and saves the result. Before you book. Aim for 85% or more on practice tests and be able to explain where each piece of data comes from.

examFormat.heading: OmniStudio Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: You can take the exam online with a proctor or at a test centre. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe something a user needs to do on screen, or data that must be fetched or saved, and ask which OmniStudio component handles it.
bestWayToPass: Learn the four tools: OmniScript for guided steps, FlexCard for displaying information, Data Mapper for reading and writing Salesforce data, Integration Procedure for server-side work.
Follow the data: Know how values pass into a component, between steps, and back out again.
Know when to go server-side: Anything heavy or involving several systems belongs in an Integration Procedure, not in the script.
Practise debugging: Use preview and the debug panel to see what data each element actually receives.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests hands-on building with OmniStudio: OmniScripts, FlexCards, Data Mappers and Integration Procedures, plus how they fit together and how to extend them with custom components. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 72% pass mark, weighted towards Omniscripts (20%) and Omnistudio Fundamentals (18%).

keyConcepts.h2: OmniStudio Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: The Four Tools and What Each Is For
blocks.body: **OmniScript** guides a user through steps on screen, collecting input and showing results, which suits processes like opening an account or changing a plan. **FlexCard** displays a compact, actionable summary of a record or customer, often as the entry point to an OmniScript. **Data Mapper** (previously DataRaptor) reads, transforms and writes Salesforce data: Extract reads records, Load writes them, Transform reshapes data without touching the database, and Turbo Extract is a faster read with fewer options. **Integration Procedure** runs server-side logic, calling several sources and combining the results in one round trip. Most exam questions reduce to choosing between these four.

blocks.heading: Data Mappers: Extract, Load and Transform
blocks.body: A **Data Mapper Extract** queries Salesforce objects and returns structured JSON, with filters and field mappings defined in configuration. A **Load** takes JSON and writes it to Salesforce objects, creating or updating records, and can handle parent and child records together. A **Transform** changes the shape of data, for example flattening a nested structure or renaming keys, without reading or writing records. **Turbo Extract** is a faster, more limited read for simple single-object cases. Formulas can be applied inside a Data Mapper for small calculations. Keeping these in configuration rather than Apex is what allows admins to change them later.

blocks.heading: Integration Procedures and Performance
blocks.body: An **Integration Procedure** runs on the server and is the right place for anything involving more than one call. Its elements include Data Mapper actions, HTTP actions to outside systems, Remote Actions to call Apex, and Response actions to shape the output. Two settings matter for speed. **Chainable** lets a long procedure continue in a separate transaction so it does not hit limits. Running elements **in parallel** lets independent calls happen at once instead of one after another. The main performance lesson for the exam is to do the work in one server-side procedure rather than making an OmniScript call out many times.

blocks.heading: OmniScript Structure and Custom Components
blocks.body: An OmniScript is built from **elements** grouped into **steps**. Input elements collect data, display elements show it, action elements fetch or save it, and **conditional views** show or hide elements based on what the user has entered. Data flows through the script's JSON, and each element reads from and writes to a named key, which is why naming matters. When the standard elements cannot do something, a **custom Lightning Web Component** can be embedded in the script and exchange data with it. OmniStudio components can also be placed on Lightning pages, in Experience Cloud sites, and called from FlexCards.

blocks.heading: Debugging, Deployment and Versioning
blocks.body: OmniStudio components are **versioned**: you activate a version, and to change it you create a new one rather than editing the active one. Preview mode and the debug panel show the JSON at each step, which is the fastest way to find out why an element received nothing. For moving between orgs, components are exported and imported as datapacks, and should be included in your release process like any other metadata. Watch for references to records by ID, which differ between orgs and are a common cause of a component working in one environment and failing in another.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce OmniStudio Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Most questions name a task and expect you to pick the tool. Ask whether the work happens on screen or on the server, and whether it reads, writes or reshapes data.

blocks.heading: OmniScript Design
blocks.body: Guided, multi-step user journeys. Use conditional views to show only what applies, and keep heavy work out of the script.

blocks.heading: Data Mappers
blocks.body: Extract reads, Load writes, Transform reshapes, Turbo Extract is a fast simple read. Keep them configurable rather than coding equivalents in Apex.

blocks.heading: Integration Procedures
blocks.body: Server-side work combining several sources in one call. Use chainable for long processing and parallel elements for independent calls.

blocks.heading: FlexCards
blocks.body: Compact summaries that display data and launch actions, often the entry point into an OmniScript.

blocks.heading: Custom LWC in OmniStudio
blocks.body: Embed a custom component when standard elements cannot do the job, and pass data in and out through the script's JSON.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio tool is used to create guided, step-by-step digital experiences?
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniScript provides declarative, step-by-step guided experiences without code.
whyWrong: LWC alone isn't OmniStudio's guided-experience tool: OmniScript is purpose-built for that.
Visualforce is a legacy Salesforce Core UI framework, not an OmniStudio tool.
Apex is a backend Salesforce Core language, not a guided-experience builder tool.

sampleQuestions.question: What is DataRaptor used for in OmniStudio?
options: Data extraction, load, and transform (DET, DLT, DTT)
sampleQuestions.explanation: DataRaptors handle data extraction (DET), load (DLT), and transform (DTT) for OmniStudio.
whyWrong: DataRaptor isn't used for sending emails, that's outside its scope.
DataRaptor doesn't send Slack messages, it handles data extract/load/transform.
DataRaptor isn't a CPQ configuration tool.

sampleQuestions.question: Which component displays a compact, card-based view of record data?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards display compact, card-based views of data with declarative layout.
whyWrong: Integration Procedure orchestrates backend logic, it isn't a visual card component.
DataRaptor moves and transforms data, it doesn't render a card-based UI.
OmniScript builds guided flows, not compact card views.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Integration Procedure in OmniStudio?
options: A reusable server-side flow that orchestrates APIs and DataRaptors
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration Procedures orchestrate server-side logic, APIs, and DataRaptors.
whyWrong: An email template is unrelated to backend orchestration logic.
A report is a Salesforce analytics artifact, not an orchestration flow.
A dashboard visualizes data, it isn't an orchestration mechanism.

sampleQuestions.question: Which industry solution commonly uses OmniStudio?
options: Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries for digital flows
sampleQuestions.explanation: OmniStudio is used across Financial Services, Insurance, and other industries for digital experiences.
whyWrong: Manufacturing isn't the typical highlighted use case for OmniStudio.
Education isn't the typical highlighted use case for OmniStudio.
Retail alone undersells OmniStudio's broader industry use across Financial Services, Insurance, and more.

sampleQuestions.question: What is DET (DataRaptor Extract) used for?
options: To extract data from Salesforce or external sources
sampleQuestions.explanation: DET extracts data from Salesforce or external sources.
whyWrong: DET is specifically for extraction, not the loading step.
DET is the extract step, not the transform step (that's DTT).
DET isn't for sending emails, it's a data extraction tool.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniScript element type defines a step?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Step and Type elements define OmniScript structure.
whyWrong: FlexCard is a separate OmniStudio component, not an OmniScript element type.
Integration Procedure is a separate OmniStudio tool, not an OmniScript element type.
DataRaptor is a separate OmniStudio tool, not an OmniScript element type.

sampleQuestions.question: What does FlexCard data source support?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexCards can use Apex, DataRaptor, or Integration Procedure.
whyWrong: FlexCard data sources include far more than 'no data' implies.
Email isn't a valid FlexCard data source.
OmniScript alone doesn't capture the range of sources FlexCards can pull from (Apex, DataRaptor, Integration Procedure).

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio feature supports conditional navigation?
whyWrong: OmniStudio does support conditional navigation; 'no support' is incorrect.
OmniScript navigation isn't limited to static, unconditional paths.
OmniScript supports branching logic, not just strictly linear flows.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of an Integration Procedure output?
options: To return data to the caller (OmniScript, FlexCard)
sampleQuestions.explanation: Integration Procedure outputs return data to callers.
whyWrong: Deleting data isn't the purpose of an Integration Procedure output.
Integration Procedure output returns data, it doesn't replace input logic.
Logging isn't the primary purpose of an Integration Procedure's output, returning data to the caller is.

sampleQuestions.question: Which deployment tool is used for OmniStudio?
sampleQuestions.explanation: FlexDeploy and source-driven deployment manage OmniStudio.
whyWrong: Change Sets are a Salesforce Core deployment mechanism, not the OmniStudio-specific approach.
Workbench is a generic Salesforce tool, not the OmniStudio-specific deployment approach.
Data Loader moves records, not OmniStudio metadata.

sampleQuestions.question: What does OmniScript Save behavior control?
options: When and how OmniScript state is persisted
whyWrong: Save behavior is distinct from navigation logic.
OmniScript Save behavior does control something specific, persistence of state, so 'nothing' is incorrect.
Save behavior is distinct from validation logic.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OmniStudio component can invoke Apex?
whyWrong: OmniScript orchestrates the guided experience but relies on Integration Procedures to invoke Apex.
FlexCard displays data, it doesn't invoke Apex directly.
DataRaptor moves/transforms data, it doesn't invoke Apex directly the way Integration Procedures can.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of FlexCard merge fields?
options: To display dynamic data from the data source
sampleQuestions.explanation: Merge fields display dynamic data in FlexCards.
whyWrong: DataRaptor is a separate tool, merge fields don't replace it.
Merge fields display data; they don't send emails.
Merge fields render data on the card; they don't generate reports.

sampleQuestions.question: Which best practice applies to OmniStudio development?
options: Reusable elements, error handling, and user testing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reusable design, error handling, and testing support quality.
whyWrong: Building for single use contradicts the reusability best practice.
Avoiding reuse leads to duplicated, harder-to-maintain solutions, the opposite of best practice.
Ignoring testing increases risk of production failures, the opposite of best practice.
